title: Why I Chose Computer Science
excerpt: A look at how I ended up deciding to study CS.
content:
It started in grade 4, where Marvin , Victor and I would write pieces on stuff we learnt while watching documentaries. Our dream was to become scientists. Over the years that passed, I stuck to the idea of becoming a scientist. But along the line I realised I wouldn't be able to be a scientist if I never commited to one branch of science. So as a lover of mathematics and logic I made the silent decision in my head to become a software engineer. This stuck with me through my high school days and when the day I was supposed to select what I wanted to do in the university, there was no doubt in my head just a clear resolve.

The Decision

You don't just jump into stuff like these you'd need to have interest in what you are doing. I remember vividly the documentary I watched that led me to make this decision. It was one about microprocessors and how they work. After watching that piece I haven't looked back ever since.

What I Learned

I've learnt a lot in my journey so far. And one realization I have made is that I am always going to be discovering something new and its in a way part of the reasons why I love what I do

My Advice

If you're just starting out, resist the urge to skip the fundamentals. Spend time learning how things work and you'll be fine provided you have passion for what you do. Build real projects. Break things. Fix them. The confidence you'll gain will make you a better developer.

title: How I Feel About Life, God, and the Universe
excerpt: A personal reflection on my beliefs, my place in the world, and my journey of self-discovery.
content:
I've always been a curious person. I love the fact that I have a little bit of knowledge about a lot of things. That curiosity has led me to some interesting places — both literally and figuratively.

My Beliefs

I am a Christian who believes in God Almighty, the power of hard work, the importance of kindness, and the value of lifelong learning. I also believe that everyone has a unique purpose in life — and it's up to each of us to discover what that purpose is. I also know for a fact that scripture has the answers to every single situation a person finds his or herself in.

My Journey

My journey has been filled with ups and downs — but I wouldn't trade it for anything. Every challenge has made me stronger, every setback has taught me a lesson, every success has motivated me to keep going, and every human interaction I've had has taught me stuff I would never have discovered about myself or the world on my own.

Looking Ahead

I'm excited about the future. I know there will be more challenges, opportunities and people I'll meet — and I'm preparing myself for whatever comes my way.

title: Hot Takes
excerpt: A collection of my hot takes on various topics.
content:
Hot Takes

This is just me saying what I feel about various social issues

    Take One

  • You are going to suffer either way, so you might as well suffer for something you believe in. People are going to have opinions about you regardless of what you do, so you might as well pursue something you are actually interested in. This applies to everything in life, from your career choices to your personal relationships. Don't let the fear of judgment hold you back from pursuing your passions. Especially on the career path you choose, many young Africans find themselves in situations where someone whether a parent, relative, or friend chooses a carreer path for them and usually it isn't something they have interest in. I say this because sometimes it is the love for what you do that keeps you going when things get tough. That and that alone and it is very disheartening to see people quit what they do just because they had no interest in whatever they were doing.

    • Take 2

  • Sometimes the thing that ruins you is knowing something you were never supposed to know about someone you love. Before that moment, everything felt simple, you trusted them, you looked at them the same wayeveryday and your brainwas calm because you believed the version of them you created in your head. But then one small truth slips out. Maybe it was a text message you weren't supposed to see, a conversation you overheard, or a confession they made in a moment of weakness. Suddenly, the image you had of them shatters, and you're left with the chilling realization that the person you thought you knew doesn't exist. Its not even about what they did anymore but the fact that you can't unsee it and the change it brings to how you view them. It makes you question every memory you have with them and whether or not they were lying the whole time.

    • Take 3

  • Don't ever hate yourself because you will treat yourself worse than anyone who ever hurt you. You'd realize that you were quicker to forgive people who offended you but have held hate for yourself to the point where you don't remember how it even started.

    • Take 4

  • You can't be mad that someone didn't act the way that you would have, at least not in the sense that the uphold values and mindsets you live by. This is just down to the simple fact that they aren't you. They haven't been shaped by the same experiences, disappointments and values you live by that will allow you to act the way you would have acted. This doesn't also excuse certain behavior

    • Take 5

  • Drop the ego and just reach out. I feel like today's society has made it look like reaching out first makes you look desperate or vulnerable. No it isn't it just confirms the fact that you are human.

    • Take 6

  • Always choose progress over perfection. Just go with small improvements instead of forcing big cahanges. Just know that small steps taken daily creates big results in the future

    • Take 7

  • The beauty of being lost is that every direction becomes a possibility

    • Take 8

  • Tearing people down because of their preference doesn't make you superioir it just makes you someone who mistakes their taste for personality. Your preferences aren't universal truths, they're just shaped by your own experiences and biases. What you find cringe someone finds joy in it. You don't judge peoples passion and the thing that make them happy because they are not what you would choose

    • Take 9

  • No one owes you anything. I say this because entitlement has prevented people from reaching the heights they were supposed because hey felt like the world "owed" them something. The truth is the only one who "owes" you something is yourself and it is a choice you make to provide whatever you owe to yourself to yourself.
